lesson.text: Quick memory: what is pixel art? (A picture made on a grid of squares.) Today: talking about art, and helping each other improve.

Feedback is what people say about your work to help you make it better. Good feedback is kind: about the work, not the person. It is specific: it says exactly what. And it is helpful: it gives an idea to try.
Use sentence starters: I like … because …, I notice …, I wonder if … or What if you tried …?

messages: I like the colours because they glow.
I notice the sky is very dark.
What if you tried a lighter sun?

lesson.text: Two stars and a wish: say two things you like, then one wish for what could be even better.
Worked example: not It's nice, but I like the bright orange sky because it feels warm. I wonder if the tree could be bigger, so it looks nearer.
Getting feedback: listen, say thank you, then choose what to change. It is your work: you decide. Leonardo da Vinci filled notebooks with sketches and drafts before he painted.
Improve, then compare: put your first draft and your new one side by side. What got better? Every draft teaches you something.
Try it in the world: visit a friend's build in your world and give two stars and a wish. Then ask for feedback on your own build, and make one change.

exercises.prompt: Which feedback is kind and helpful?
exercises.hint: Is it about the work? Does it give an idea?
choices: I love the colours. Could the tree be taller?
exercises.explain: It says what works and gives an idea to try: kind and helpful.

exercises.prompt: Feedback should be about the work, not the person.
exercises.explain: True: talk about the picture or the build, never about the person.

exercises.prompt: Sort these: helpful feedback or not?
items: I like how you shaded the ball.
I wonder if the sky could be bluer.
What if you added a bird?
exercises.hint: Does it say something specific, or give an idea?
exercises.explain: Helpful: shading, a bluer sky, a bird. Not helpful: comparing, one word, no idea.

exercises.prompt: What should you say when someone gives you feedback?
exercises.hint: They took time to help you.
exercises.explain: Say thank you, then choose what to change.

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence starter to what it does.
exercises.hint: Liking, noticing and wondering do different jobs.
exercises.explain: I like says what works, I notice what you see, I wonder gives an idea; two stars and a wish does all three.

choices: The shadow under the ball looks real.
exercises.explain: It names exactly what works: the shadow under the ball.

exercises.prompt: Put the steps of giving feedback in order.
exercises.hint: Look before you speak; listen at the end.
items: Ask a question or share an idea
Say what you like and why
exercises.explain: Look, say what you like, share an idea, then listen.

exercises.prompt: What does two stars and a wish mean?
exercises.hint: Stars are for what you like.
choices: two things you like and one idea
exercises.explain: Two stars: two things you like. A wish: one idea to make it better.

exercises.prompt: When you get feedback, you must change everything they said.
exercises.explain: False: listen and say thank you, then you decide what to change.

exercises.prompt: Zara says: Your castle is boring. How could she say it more helpfully?
exercises.hint: Change it into an idea to try.
choices: I wonder if a tall tower would help.
exercises.explain: I wonder if a tall tower would help. gives a kind idea about the work.

choices: each draft can improve on the last
exercises.explain: Each draft is a chance to try ideas and feedback, and improve.

items: the eyes are a bit high
exercises.explain: Specific: the sky, the tree, the eyes. Vague: nice, cool, good job.

exercises.prompt: Kind feedback can still suggest a change.
exercises.hint: Think of two stars and a wish.
exercises.explain: True: the wish is a kind idea for a change.

exercises.prompt: You get feedback: I wonder if the sea could be bluer. You like your green sea. What can you do?
choices: say thank you and keep it
exercises.explain: Say thank you. It is your work, so you can keep your green sea.

exercises.prompt: Match each comment on a drawing to what kind of feedback it is.
items: The shadow makes it look round.
matches: a wish: an idea to try
exercises.hint: Is it about the work or the person? Does it say exactly what? Does it give an idea?
exercises.explain: The shadow comment is a star: it names exactly what works. The bluer sky is a wish: an idea to try. 'It's nice' is vague. 'You can't draw' is unkind, because it is about the person, not the work.
